clue.text: Oddly, I err repeatedly with this breed

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters behave strangely, so they are rearranged
repeatedly says the words I err are used twice over

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone keeps making mistakes with a strange dog breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles I ERR to IERRIERR; add THIS, and 'Oddly' rearranges the twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish terrier is a recognised dog breed, a red-coated terrier from Ireland.

clue.text: Frozen mass of rocks on mountain

parts.note: drinks served on the rocks come with ice cubes, so rocks means ice
berg is a mountain, as in South Africa's Drakensberg

explanation.surface: A geological description of an icy lump of rock sitting on a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge floating block of ice broken off a glacier is a frozen mass.

clue.text: Two or three, for example? Not half

definitions.meaning: two and three are examples of whole numbers
a whole number is never a fraction such as a half

explanation.surface: A puzzle about numbers, with a dismissive aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole numbers such as two or three are this, and a whole number is by definition never a fraction like one half.

clue.text: Vital sign in the area damaged around disease

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters wrap round the disease abbreviation
damaged letters are broken up and reassembled in a new order

parts.note: TB is short for tuberculosis, a disease

explanation.surface: A medic notes a pulse in a region ravaged by illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vital sign' is the definition, not 'disease'; 'damaged' rearranges THE AREA, and 'around' wraps those letters round the disease.
explanation.definitionFit: The pulse a doctor checks is one of the body's vital signs.

clue.text: Doors people are going to use

definitions.text: Doors people are going to use

parts.words: Doors people are going to use
parts.note: read as the doors through which people go out of a building

explanation.surface: Instructions about which doors a crowd will use.
explanation.definitionFit: Doors marked for leaving a building are its ways out.

clue.text: Forbear's burden

definitions.meaning: to forbear is to abstain from doing something
an old sense of burden is the chorus repeated in a song

explanation.surface: An ancestor's heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to hold back from doing something, and a burden is the repeated chorus of a song.

clue.text: Person who gets away with extremely egregious prank

indicators.note: extremely picks the very ends of the word egregious, its first and last letters

parts.note: a caper is a playful prank or escapade

explanation.surface: A prankster gets off scot-free after an outrageous stunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who flees captivity or escapes from a place is a runaway.

clue.text: Cheat with lightly cooked piece in national dish

parts.note: to welsh is to cheat by not paying a debt
rare meat is only lightly cooked
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A fraudster hides an underdone portion inside a country's signature meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese on toast, known by this name, is a traditional dish associated with Wales.

clue.text: Some select radio for classical drama

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Choosing a radio station that broadcasts ancient plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is a Greek tragedy by Sophocles, a classic of ancient theatre.

clue.text: Taints female trapped in depraved sin, etc.

indicators.note: trapped in means one piece is held inside another
depraved means corrupted or twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman caught up in a life of vice and so on is corrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depraved' rearranges SIN ETC into INECTS, and 'trapped in' sets F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To taint something is to contaminate or pollute it, as germs do.

clue.text: Put an end to whipping device unknown here — it's still produced up North

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to put an end to it
a whisk is a kitchen tool for whipping cream or eggs
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Abolish a flogging instrument nobody has heard of round here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' is the distilling apparatus, not 'yet'; Scotland is up North in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt spirit distilled in Scotland comes out of a pot still.

clue.text: Hunt the poet in way that's cunning

indicators.note: in means the poet's first name goes inside the abbreviation for way

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
Leigh Hunt was an English Romantic poet and essayist

explanation.surface: A call to track down a poet by some crafty route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunt' looks like a verb but is the surname of Leigh Hunt, friend of Keats and Shelley.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means craft or trickery, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: Application of shock treatment

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mop, so this is something applied to treat the hair

explanation.surface: A grim medical procedure involving electric shocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair wash is applied to a mop of hair to clean it.

clue.text: Bring back Gregory's middle name

indicators.note: bring back tells us to take the letters in reverse order
middle picks the inside letters of the word, dropping its first and last

explanation.surface: A request to revive Gregory's second name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle' takes REGOR from GREGORY, and 'Bring back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common English male first name.

clue.text: Entire 300 defective — that's odd

indicators.note: defective means faulty, so the letters are broken and rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, so three of them make 300

explanation.surface: A whole batch of three hundred items turns out faulty, which is strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unconventional or peculiar is described as odd.

clue.text: Sailors from Irish port needed to get wine out

parts.note: Cork is a port in southern Ireland, here with a possessive 's: sailors from there belong to Cork
the crew of a ship are its sailors

explanation.surface: Seamen from an Irish harbour are needed to unload a wine shipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors from Cork are Cork's crew; Cork is a port city in the south of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral opener is the tool you need to pull the stopper from a bottle.

clue.text: It doesn't rise in spring, it comes down in fall

definitions.text: It doesn't rise in spring, it comes down in fall

parts.words: It doesn't rise in spring, it comes down in fall
parts.note: read as a liquid that does not well up from a spring in the ground but falls from the sky

explanation.surface: Something seasonal that stays low in spring and drops in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Water collected from showers falls from clouds rather than bubbling up from underground.

clue.text: African or Russian removing capital from part of Western Europe

indicators.note: removing capital means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a Liberian is an African; a Siberian, a Russian, works equally well

explanation.surface: A nationality puzzle comparing someone from Africa or Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: Either LIBERIAN or SIBERIAN loses its first letter to give the same result.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula holding Spain and Portugal gives this adjective for things from that part of Europe.

clue.text: Feeble nuclear group as source of power

parts.note: wet is British slang for feeble or weak
a cell has a nucleus, and also means a small group of activists

explanation.surface: A weak band of nuclear activists as an energy supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery with liquid electrolyte supplies electrical energy.

clue.text: Disgusted reaction from dramatist after play's opening

indicators.note: after says the dramatist's name follows the opening letter
the opening of the play is its first letter

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A critic's scornful response from a playwright after a first night.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old exclamation of contempt or impatience.

clue.text: Illusion harboured by orphan tomboy

indicators.note: harboured by means the answer is sheltered within the following words

explanation.surface: A false belief held by a parentless tomboy.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostly apparition is something unreal, a figment.

clue.text: Islander in a hat I altered

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An islander wears a modified hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Haiti, a Caribbean island nation, is an islander.

clue.text: Having complaint, this encourages appetite, initially

definitions.text: Having complaint, this encourages appetite, initially

parts.note: a beef is a grievance or complaint

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A remedy for someone poorly that whets the appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, the clue describes a savoury broth once given to invalids to stimulate the appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat broth was traditionally served to sick people to restore their appetite.

clue.text: Rained less, totally missing odd parts in mountains

indicators.note: dropping the first, third, fifth letters and so on leaves only the even ones

explanation.surface: A weather report: less rain over the peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The great range running down western South America is a chain of mountains.

clue.text: His law I translated into this language

indicators.note: translated suggests a change of form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's law rendered into a foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiswahili is a Bantu language widely spoken in East Africa.

clue.text: Following reserves, I advance in the rear

indicators.note: following says the next piece comes after the reserves abbreviation

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's army reserve
to advance money is to lend it

explanation.surface: Behind the reserve troops, a soldier moves up at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The final or hindmost part of something is its back end.

clue.text: A second opinion about feeble king

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a thin excuse is a feeble one
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Getting another view on a weak monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconsidering a matter means forming a fresh view on it.

clue.text: Mixed in among Welsh, female of other sort

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman of a different nationality mingles with Welsh people.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman from England is a female of a nationality other than Welsh.
